The brain of the project: runs the code, has WiFi and Bluetooth.
A module with a metal can printed ESP-32, BOOT and EN buttons, and a micro-USB port. In this photo it is plugged into the expansion board.
Where the ESP32 plugs in. Makes wiring easier and supplies power.
A black board printed ESP32 ESP32S 30P Expansion board. Every GPIO has a G/V/S pin row, plus a 3.3V/5V selector jumper.
A board with holes for building circuits without soldering.
White board with 400 holes. The red and blue lines at the edge are the power rails.
Connects components to each other.
Three kinds: male-male, male-female, female-female. They can be torn off one by one from the bundle.
Supplies power and uploads code from the laptop to the ESP32.
Check that the small end fits the ESP32's micro-USB port. (The small item in the middle of the photo is the LDR.)
Limits current or divides voltage.
A small blue cylinder with colour bands. The colours show the value. Not polarised.
A small light used as an indicator.
Polarised: long leg = + (anode), short leg and the flat side of the body = − (cathode). Always use a resistor.
Makes a beep for warnings.
A black cylinder with a hole on top. The + leg is usually longer, or there is a + mark on the body.
Light sensor: its resistance drops when it is bright.
A small disc with a winding line pattern and two long legs. Not polarised.
Air temperature and humidity sensor.
A blue box with holes and 4 legs: VCC, DATA, (empty), GND.
A resistor whose value is set by turning it. Here it is for the LCD contrast.
A metal body with a rotating shaft and 3 legs. A marking like B10K means 10 kΩ.
A 2-row display, 16 characters each.
16 pin holes numbered 1 to 16 along the bottom edge. A pin header must be soldered on first.
A row of pins to solder onto the LCD.
A black strip with gold pins. It can be snapped to the number you need (16 for the LCD).
A push button for input.
Some are big (12 mm) and some small (6 mm). 4 legs, connected in pairs inside.
A distance sensor using sound waves, roughly 2–400 cm.
A blue board with two cylindrical "eyes". Pins: VCC, Trig, Echo, GND.
A motor that can be turned to a set angle, 0–180°.
A blue box with 3 wires: brown = GND, red = 5V, orange/yellow = signal.
Attached to the servo shaft to move something.
A white plastic piece with holes, plus a small screw.
A switch controlled by the ESP32 to turn other devices on.
A blue box printed SRD-05VDC. Pins IN, GND, VCC; screw terminals COM, NO, NC. Do not use it with 220V mains yet.
